transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-04 10:00 UTC — Duration: ~60 minutes. Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (DataHaven SRE), Ethan Cole (DataHaven ML Eng), Sarah Lin (DataHaven Security)

00:00 - Avery Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
00:05 - Maya Patel: Maya here, SRE at DataHaven.
00:07 - Ethan Cole: Ethan on the ML side.
00:09 - Sarah Lin: Sarah from security.
:11 - Diego Martinez: diego here from redwood se, thanks all.

01:00 - Avery Chen: quick agenda — networking updates, perf bench results, driver/AMI upgrade, security check, next steps. anything else?
01:12 - Maya Patel: no that's it. the big pain is the intermittent routing flaps we saw last week after the peering change, which impacted p95.

03:15 - Diego Martinez: yea from our side the logs showed a mix of pathing — some requests were routed to the fallback region and that created extra hops and serialization overhead. also noticed kernel driver mismatch on the pilot nodes, the nvidia driver was at 525.x while runtime expects 540.x so that explains some perf regressions.

05:30 - Ethan Cole: hmm that could explain token throughput drop. my runs showed steady p50 but p95 spikes to 1.2s for 512 tokens, which is more than expected.

07:12 - Maya Patel: we sent flow logs — NAT translation counts were high during the time windows. can we avoid egress through NAT for inference instances?

09:00 - Diego Martinez: yes we recommend using private link style peering or an explicit route so inference agents don't hairpin through NAT; that reduces RTT. also enabling prefix caching on the runtime will help with cold-starts.

11:45 - Sarah Lin: security note — we need to confirm KMS key usage for model artifacts and audit log retention policy. we cannot keep logs beyond 90 days without a compliance ticket.

14:20 - Avery Chen: understood. we support customer-managed KMS and can rotate keys; we'll share the security checklist. Diego, can you call out the driver upgrade plan?

15:10 - Diego Martinez: sure — recommended path: replace AMI with our validated AMI that has driver 540.x + cuda 12.x. steps: snapshot, launch AMI in staging, run bench, do canary, then rollout. small caveat: if customer has locked kernel modules or custom nvidia packages, need to coordinate.

18:40 - Ethan Cole: on the benchmark side i ran the toy workload — default batch size 8, kv cache off. when i re-ran with kv cache on we saw 15% token/sec improvement. with driver bump we expect more. want to run 1M token run next week to get stable p95 numbers.

22:00 - Maya Patel: network — we also saw route table async propagation delays. could be AWS eventual consistency after peering changes. we reverted a route earlier which seemed to stabilize traffic.

24:30 - Diego Martinez: fwiw we recommend setting a static route preference and using health-based routing for failover. also set route table propagation checks in terraform apply to avoid surprises.

27:10 - Sarah Lin: do we have an enterprise fallback plan if private deployment has sustained perf issues? we discussed Dedicated fallback last week.

28:00 - Avery Chen: yes, Dedicated as a short-term fallback — we can provision dedicated capacity in region for a limited window; we'll send cost delta. idea is canary on dedicated while you resolve on-prem issues.

31:20 - Ethan Cole: curious about KV cache invalidation — what happens on model rollouts?

32:10 - Diego Martinez: when you pin model version we keep KV cache stable; during rollouts we use versioned cache keys and gradual migration, so you shouldn't see mass invalidation. we'll share design doc.

35:00 - Maya Patel: can you share the exact AMI IDs that have been validated? we need them for our infra approval process.

36:05 - Diego Martinez: yes — will send list in follow-up, includes AMI-Redwood-540x-2025-05 and AMI-Redwood-540x-2025-05-small. note names may be slighted by naming convention in your account.

38:40 - Sarah Lin: audit logs question — do you push logs to customer S3 or do we pull? we prefer push with server-side encryption using our KMS key.

40:00 - Avery Chen: recommended pattern: we push compressed audit logs to your S3 with SSE-KMS using your key; we can rotate. will include retention config.

42:50 - Maya Patel: on the perf tests, i'll run two configs — current baseline and with driver/AMI + kv cache + static routes. we'll time p50/p95 and token throughput.

45:10 - Ethan Cole: i hit an error in one of the stress runs — OOM on sequence length 2048 when batch size 16. suspect quantization profile mismatch.

46:20 - Diego Martinez: ok we need to check the quantization profile used by your load; if you used int4 and a non-validated kernel, that can blow memory patterns. suggest lowering batch or enabling dynamic batching. also we'll share recommended quant profiles.

49:00 - Sarah Lin: re compliance — we need to confirm the pilot data classification and whether model outputs get stored long-term. currently we set ephemeral storage for outputs.

50:15 - Avery Chen: we can keep outputs ephemeral by default; if you want long-term storage we can integrate with your S3 and apply lifecycle. we'll make that an explicit opt-in.

52:30 - Maya Patel: ok quick recap of blockers: routing flaps/peering propagation, driver mismatch, and a couple quant/profile config items. action items and owners?

54:00 - Avery Chen: i'll recap and put dates — Diego to share AMI + driver steps, i'll send network diagram and SOW, Maya and Ethan run benchmarks, Sarah confirm KMS scope.

56:40 - Ethan Cole: also can we schedule a 30-minute deep-dive specifically on routing and failover with our infra team next week?

57:00 - Avery Chen: yes propose Wed 2025-06-09 14:00 UTC, we'll send invite.

59:10 - Maya Patel: thanks everyone, if no other items we'll close.

59:45 - Avery Chen: thanks all, notes and action items in follow-up email. bye.

End of transcript. Some automatic captions had small name mismatches and punctuation errors.
